answer: Cheap aliases flood a market if a new name is only a signed paragraph. Enrollment needs a field proof: compose a 14-line sonnet, then visit a paper atlas desk and press a 40-gram calcite coupon into a numbered karst well whose conductivity is published every 15 minutes. The memo stores SHA-256(page_id || well_id || conductivity_bin || address). Peers reread the well log and reject a coupon off by more than 0.3 mS, or a page_id reused this epoch. The trip costs 2.1 hours plus 19 POA for the coupon. If the well is dry or the hash collides, the coupon is void and the address waits two epochs.
